::: {.fi-standfirst}
Most tools hand you an evidence map and stop. **FRESH** works the harder problem:
what to do when the credible sources disagree with each other. It audits what
published studies actually support once trial quality and pooled effects are
re-checked, reconciles expert rating systems that contradict each other, estimates
risk for subgroups instead of national averages, and carries measurement error
through to the number you finally read. The same machinery scores well-being across
the domains that make up a life, sleep and movement and mind and social connection
alongside diet, drawing on self-report, wearables, and biomarkers, with the doubt
kept on the face of the score.

Food is where the methods get proven, because that is where expert systems clash
most openly and public belief drifts furthest from the evidence. The wager is
broader. Health effort pours into changing behavior and widening access while the
information itself gets treated as settled, and it is not settled. Better
information cures nothing on its own, but it is the cheapest lever nobody is
pulling, and people cannot decide well on a question the experts have not agreed
on. These essays are where that work goes public.
:::
